chunks: Ibn Maskan narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Nājiyah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about someone who spends the nights of Minā in Makkah. He said: "He must slaughter three sheep."

key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, instead of staying in Minā
key_terms.لَيَالِيَ: the nights referred to in the rite of staying at Minā
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the hajj location where pilgrims are to remain on designated nights
key_terms.يَذْبَحُهُنَّ: he slaughters them, meaning he offers them as sacrificial animals
key_terms.ٱلْغَنَمِ: sheep or small livestock to be offered as sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who spends the nights of Minā in Makkah during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a pilgrim who spends the nights of Minā in Makkah instead of remaining in Minā. The ruling states that such a person must offer three sheep as a sacrificial penalty.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3007 - Ibn Maskan narrated from Ja’far ibn Najiyah, from Abu Abdullah (as):

I asked him about someone who spends the nights of Mina in Mecca.
Imam (as) replied: "He must offer three sheep as a sacrifice."
